repositories.readme:
# Chronicles of the Realm · 江山时序

English · 简体中文 (Chinese) · 繁體中文 (Traditional Chinese) · 日本語 (Japanese)

**An Interactive Historical Atlas of China from the Warring States (403 BCE) to the Present — Scrub Through Time, Trace Ancient Cities, and Walk in the Footsteps of History** [**Play Live Demo (English UI) → https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en**](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en) *The story behind it (in Chinese): [From textbook maps to 1k GitHub stars](https://deanchen.me/history/atlas/2026/10/25/jiangshan-map-story.html)*

--- ## Why It's Fun to Explore Have you ever wondered while reading Chinese history or classical poetry: - *"Where exactly on today's map are Jiankang (the Six Dynasties capital), Huangzhou (where Su Dongpo composed the Red Cliffs Rhapsody in exile), Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains (where Han Yu halted his horse in the snow), or Zhuxianzhen (Yue Fei's northern campaign frontier)?"* - *"How many names did Chang'an hold across two millennia, and what pivotal events unfolded on that soil?"* - *"How did the realm evolve step by step—from the Partition of Jin and the Seven Warring States at the opening of Sima Guang's Zizhi Tongjian (403 BCE), Qin's unification campaigns, Emperor Wu of Han opening the Hexi Corridor, High Tang's Four Garrisons of Anxi, and Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan jurisdiction over Tibet, to Zeng Jize's recovery of Ili (1881 CE) and the 20th-century shift from the 'Begonia Leaf' (秋海棠) map to the 'Rooster' (雄鸡) map?"* **Chronicles of the Realm (`jiangshan-map`)** brings together **2,400+ years** of Chinese history across **18 historical periods** into a single interactive parchment atlas—featuring **multi-stage territorial and prefecture snapshots**, **ancient cities**, **strategic mountain passes**, **poetic and battlefield landmarks**, **chronological milestones**, and **reigning monarchs & imperial eras**. No heavy print atlases required—just drag the timeline and click any city to travel through space and time. --- ### Feature 1: Scrub the Timeline to Watch Realms Rise & Fall, Track Monarchs, and Compare Ancient & Modern Borders - **Multi-Polity Confrontations on a Single Canvas**: From the Seven Warring States (Qin, Chu, Qi, Yan, Zhao, Wei, Han) alongside Zhou, Yue, Ba-Shu, Zhongshan, and Yiqu, to the Three Kingdoms warlords (Yuan Shao, Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan, Gongsun's Liaodong), Northern & Southern Dynasties, Five Dynasties & Ten Kingdoms, and Song, Liao, Western Xia, Dali, Jin, and the Mongols—all rendered side-by-side in high-contrast traditional parchment hues. Hover over any polity in the bottom-left legend to highlight its territory, or click to open that polity's profile (lifespan, capitals and a short history) and zoom to its territory. - **Multi-Stage Territorial Evolution & Dashed "Ghost Boundary Diffs"**: At every major territorial milestone—such as Qin's conquest of Ba-Shu (316 BCE), Yan General Qin Kai's expansion into Liaodong (300 BCE), Ma Yuan's bronze pillars in Jiaozhi (43 CE), Sima Yi's campaign in Liaodong (238 CE), Li Jing's conquest of Tuyuhun (635 CE), the Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance's campaign in Central India (648 CE), Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan rule over Tibet (1288 CE), Ming's Jiaozhi Province in Annam (1407 CE), the 1881 Treaty of Saint Petersburg recovering Ili, the 1898 foreign leased territories, the 1945 retrocession of Taiwan, and the 1946 transition from the **"Begonia Leaf" (秋海棠)** map to the **"Rooster" (雄鸡)** map—click any milestone or phase dot to switch maps and reveal the previous phase's dashed vermilion **Ghost Boundary Diff** so territorial gains and losses are immediately visible. - **Reigning Monarch on the Timeline**: The bubble above the timeline names the monarch on the throne in the current year (e.g. `100 BCE · Western Han · Emp. Wu`, `630 CE · Tang · Emp. Taizong`, `1700 CE · Qing · Kangxi Emp. (Shengzu)`); the Chinese interface also shows the regnal era year (`唐太宗·贞观四年`). - **Ancient Prefecture Hover Inspection & Modern Province Overlay**: First-level administrative divisions (Commanderies, Circuits, Routes, and Provinces) are rendered with deduplicated **Parchment Casing** borders. Zoom in and hover over any prefecture (e.g., Ming `Yingtian Prefecture` or Three Kingdoms `Jingzhou`) to inspect its jurisdiction and modern provincial equivalents. In the top-right **Layers** menu, `Provinces` (on by default) draws today's provincial boundaries over the historical map, and `Prov. Names` adds their names. - **Dynamic River Courses, Ancient Lakes & Grand Engineering Works**: As you scrub through time, historical shifts of the Yellow River, expanding and shrinking ancient lakes (*Yunmeng Marsh*, *Lop Nur / Puchanghai*), Warring States/Qin/Han/Ming Great Walls, Sui-Tang & Grand Canals, the Silk Road, and Zheng He's maritime routes evolve in lockstep with each era; ancient coastlines around the Bohai Gulf, northern Jiangsu, the Yangtze estuary, and the Pearl River Delta also advance and retreat by era. - **Zoomable Timeline**: Drag the handles at either end of the timeline inward to zoom into one stretch of history (handy for short eras such as Qin, the Three Kingdoms, or the Five Dynasties); double-click the timeline to return to the full overview. - **Voice Narration**: Turn on the narration toggle next to the play button and autoplay reads out each year and its events in the browser's built-in voice; it also follows a person's chronicle on autoplay (requires a browser with speech synthesis). > [Try It Live: Ming Dynasty Yongle 13 (1415 CE) · Two Capitals, Thirteen Provinces & "Yingtian Prefecture" Inspection →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1415&zoom=1.75¢er=115.8,33.2&hover=Yingtian%20Prefecture&lang=en) ![Ming Dynasty 1415 CE · Yingtian Prefecture Hover Preview](assets/preview_1415_ming_yingtian_en.webp) --- ### Feature 2: Click Any Ancient City or Strategic Pass to Uncover 2,400 Years of History (`Trace Place`) **Click any ancient city or mountain pass** on the map (or double-click anywhere on the canvas) to open its **Trace Place** genealogy card: - **Bilingual City Lore Banner & 2,400-Year Administrative Genealogy**: At the top of the card, read a curated **poetic epigraph and historical biography** for the city; below, trace how its name and administrative jurisdiction evolved across all 18 historical eras—from Warring States and Qin commanderies, Han regional inspectorates, Tang circuits, and Song routes to Yuan/Ming/Qing provinces and modern municipalities—complete with `Capital` badges and dynastic seat remarks. - **Site-Specific Landmark Events**: Beneath each dynasty row, inspect major historical events that took place right on that spot (e.g., *Shang Yang's Reforms* and *Qin's Unification* at Xianyang, *Guan Yu Flooding the Seven Armies* at Fancheng, the *Xuanwu Gate Incident* at Chang'an, or *Yue Fei's Martyrdom* at Lin'an). Click the **`Chronicles`** pill in the top-right of the card to filter for dynasties with major events, and click any event to time-travel straight to that year! - **Strategic Mountain Passes & Poetic / Battlefield Landmarks**: Explore famous mountain passes—including *Hangu Pass*, *Tongguan*, *Jianmen Pass*, *Yanmen Pass*, *Yumen Pass*, *Yangguan*, and *Shanhai Pass*—rendered with traditional *Hanque* gatehouse icons and strategic terrain notes, alongside famous battlefields and literary landmarks such as *Red Cliffs (Chibi)*, *Gaixia*, *Wuzhang Plains*, *Orchid Pavilion (Lanting)*, *Yueyang Tower*, *Pavilion of Prince Teng*, *Languan Pass*, *Loulan*, *Lop Nur*, and *Issyk-Kul*. > [Try It Live: High Tang Kaiyuan 29 (741 CE) · Open Chang'an's 2,400-Year Genealogy Card →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=741&place=Chang'an&lang=en) ![High Tang 741 CE · Chang'an Trace Place & Key Events](assets/preview_741_tang_trace_en.webp) --- ### Feature 3: Person Chronicles — Trace Any Historical Figure Across Time & Space Click the top-left **Universal Search Box** (with a rotatable `e.g.` figure preview and quick-search chips, or type any monarch, general, statesman, monk, or poet such as `Cao Cao`, `Huo Qubing`, `Sima Qian`, `Yue Fei`, or `Zheng He`) to open **Person Chronicle (`点人溯事`)**, marking every milestone of their life with numbered pins across changing dynastic borders: - **Qin Shi Huang's Unification Campaigns (238–221 BCE)**: From suppressing the rebellion at Xianyang and Wang Jian's attack on Ye, to the fall of Han, Zhao, Yan, Wei, Chu, and Dai, culminating in the surrender of Qi at Linzi—as you advance stop by stop, watch the six rival kingdoms merge into the Qin Empire right on the map! - **Zhang Qian's Mission to the Western Regions (138–126 BCE)**: Depart Chang'an, endure over a decade of Xiongnu captivity without surrendering the Han imperial staff, and blaze the trail to Dayuan (Fergana), Kangju, and the Greater Yuezhi. - **Zhuge Liang's Emergence & Northern Expeditions (207–234 CE)**: From the Three Visits at Longzhong and the alliance at Chaisang before Red Cliffs, to entering Shu, the White Emperor City entrustment, the Southern Campaign across the Lu River, Hanzhong's *Memorial on Deploying the Troops*, Mount Qi, and the autumn winds of Wuzhang Plains. - **Xuanzang's Pilgrimage to India (627–645 CE)**: Slip past Yumen Pass alone across the Moheyan Desert, scale the icy Bedel Pass, cross the Indus, study at Nalanda Monastery, and debate at Kanyakubja (Kanauj) before returning to Chang'an. - **Li Bai's Grand Travels Across Tang China (701–762 CE)**: From Suyab and boyhood in Shu, sailing out through the Three Gorges at twenty-four, scattering gold in Yangzhou, serving in the Hanlin Academy at Chang'an, meeting Du Fu in Luoyang, receiving amnesty at White Emperor City, to his final years at Dangtu. - **Su Shi's Literary Exile Across Song China (1056–1101 CE)**: From leaving Meishan for the capital Kaifeng and gazing at the moon in Mizhou, to composing the *Red Cliffs Rhapsody* in Huangzhou exile, Huizhou, and crossing the sea to Danzhou on Hainan Island. - **Wang Yangming's Unity of Knowledge & Action (1472–1529 CE)**: From birth in Yuyao and imprisonment in Beijing, to his enlightenment at Longchang in Guizhou, pacifying bandits in Southern Ganzhou, capturing the rebel Prince of Ning in 35 days, teaching at the Tianquan Bridge in Shaoxing, and his final words *"This mind is bright and clear; what more is there to say?"* at Nan'an. - **Multi-Person Chronicles**: Type two or three names into the search box (e.g. `Li Bai, Du Fu, Gao Shi` or `Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan`) to merge their journeys onto one timeline. Places where they met in the same year are marked as shared encounters, and the `Shared N` pill narrows the list to just those stops. - **Event Storylines**: Major events unfold stop by stop, just like a person's life. The Chu–Han Contention (207–202 BCE), the An Lushan Rebellion (755–763 CE) and the Jingkang Catastrophe (1125–1142 CE) are each laid out in ten stops across three acts, with the two sides drawn in different colors so each side's advances are easy to follow. Each time you step to the next event (`‹ / ›`, `← / →`, or `Space` to auto-play), **the timeline year, reigning monarch, imperial era, and dynastic territories evolve in sync with their footsteps**, highlighting the active transition arc alongside bilingual primary-source excerpts and poems written at that exact site. > [Try It Live: Su Dongpo's Life & Exile Across Song China (1037–1101 CE) →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=sushi&lang=en) ![Person Chronicle · Su Shi's Life & Exile Route](assets/preview_journey_sushi_en.webp) --- ### Feature 4: Easter Egg · Map Pinpoint Challenge — What Imperial Court Rank Would You Earn? Think you know Chinese historical geography? Click **`Quiz ›`** in the corner of the **Universal Search Box** guide bar (or type `quiz` for **`Map Pinpoint · Ancient Place Quiz`**): - **Dynastic Historical Clues + Blind Map Pinpointing**: City labels are hidden while the prompt asks you to locate an ancient city across a 10-round progressive difficulty deck—accompanied by **dynastic historical clues** (without spoiling the modern city name). Drop your pin to preview and adjust, click the **`Confirm ↵`** chip next to the pin to lock in your answer with concentric distance score rings, and earn points based on great-circle distance to the true coordinates! - Complete 10 rounds to receive a traditional imperial cartographic title such as **Grand Historian & Master Cartographer (太史令 · 舆图大家)**, **Director of the Bureau of Operations (职方郎中)**, or **Prefectural Retainer (州郡从事)**. > [Try It Live: Western Han Emperor Wu, Yuanshou 2 (121 BCE) · Start the Map Pinpoint Challenge →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en) ![Western Han 121 BCE · Map Pinpoint Challenge Preview](assets/preview_quiz_challenge_en.webp) --- ## Keyboard Shortcuts & Shareable Deep Links ### Keyboard Shortcuts | Key / Action | Effect | | :--- | :--- | | **`/`** or **`Cmd/Ctrl + K`** | Focus the **Universal Search Box**: search **historical figures** (`Qin Shi Huang`/`Zhang Qian`/`Su Shi`), **ancient & modern cities** (`Xianyang`/`Chang'an`/`Luoyang`/`Kaifeng`), **reigning monarchs** (`Emperor Wu of Han`/`Taizong of Tang`/`Liu Che`/`Li Shimin`), **imperial eras** (`Zhenguan`/`Yongle`/`Kangxi`), **poetic & battlefield landmarks** (`Red Cliffs`/`Wuzhang Plains`/`Languan`/`Lanting`), **mountain passes** (`Hangu Pass`/`Jianmen Pass`/`Yumen Pass`), **historical events**, or the **Ancient Place Quiz** | | **`←` / `→`** or bottom **`‹ / ›`** | Jump to the previous / next historical phase, milestone event, or person event stop (hold `Shift + ← / →` to step by `10` years) | | **`Space`** | Auto-play / pause timeline evolution (or auto-advance stops in Person Chronicle mode) | | **`Esc`** | Close active popups/cards, clear search highlights, or exit custom multi-stop routes | | **`Single-click city` / `Double-click map`** | Open the 18-era **Trace Place & Key Events** genealogy card for that location | | **`Hover / Click legend swatch`** | Hover to isolate & highlight that polity's territory; click to open its profile and zoom to its territory | ### Shareable Deep Links Append query parameters to share any historical moment, battle, city genealogy, or multi-stop route: - **Jump to a specific year or territorial shift**: [`?year=-403&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-403&lang=en) (403 BCE · Partition of Jin) / [`?year=-121&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&lang=en) (121 BCE · Huo Qubing opens the Hexi Corridor) / [`?year=648&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=648&lang=en) (648 CE · Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance in India) / [`?year=1288&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1288&lang=en) (1288 CE · Yuan Xuanzhengyuan over Tibet) / [`?year=1881&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1881&lang=en) (1881 CE · Zeng Jize recovers Ili) / [`?year=1945&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1945&lang=en) (1945 CE · Retrocession of Taiwan) - **Pinpoint a famous battle**: [`?year=-260&place=长平&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-260&place=长平&lang=en) (Battle of Changping) / [`?year=208&place=赤壁&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=208&place=赤壁&lang=en) (Battle of Red Cliffs) / [`?year=383&place=淝水&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=383&place=淝水&lang=en) (Battle of Fei River) - **Inspect a city's 2,400-year genealogy**: [`?year=741&place=长安&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=741&place=长安&lang=en) (Chang'an / Xi'an) / [`?year=1415&place=应天府&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1415&place=应天府&lang=en) (Jiankang / Yingtian / Nanjing) / [`?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en) (Han Yu at Languan Pass) - **Plot a custom poetic or campaign route**: [`?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en) (Du Fu's 763 CE homeward route) / [`?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en) (Su Shi's multi-year exile route across Huzhou, Huangzhou, Huizhou, and Danzhou) - **Open a person's spatio-temporal chronicle**: [`?person=qinshihuang&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=qinshihuang&lang=en) (Qin Shi Huang) / [`?person=zhangqian&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=zhangqian&lang=en) (Zhang Qian) / [`?person=zhugeliang&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=zhugeliang&lang=en) (Zhuge Liang) / [`?person=xuanzang&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=xuanzang&lang=en) (Xuanzang) / [`?person=libai&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=libai&lang=en) (Li Bai) / [`?person=sushi&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=sushi&lang=en) (Su Shi) / [`?person=wangyangming&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=wangyangming&lang=en) (Wang Yangming) - **Compare several people or follow an event**: [`?person=libai,dufu&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=libai,dufu&lang=en) (Li Bai & Du Fu) / [`?person=caocao,liubei,sunquan&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=caocao,liubei,sunquan&lang=en) (Cao Cao, Liu Bei & Sun Quan) / [`?event=qintongyi&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?event=qintongyi&lang=en) (Qin's Conquest of the Six States) / [`?event=chuhan&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?event=chuhan&lang=en) (Chu–Han Contention) / [`?event=anshi&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?event=anshi&lang=en) (An Lushan Rebellion) / [`?event=jingkang&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?event=jingkang&lang=en) (Jingkang Catastrophe) - **Start a quiz round**: [`?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en) (Map Pinpoint Challenge) - **Switch UI language**: [`?lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en) (English) / [`?lang=zh-tw`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=zh-tw) (Traditional Chinese) / [`/`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/) (Simplified Chinese) ### Embed in Your Page Put any view of the atlas into a blog post, Notion page, or course site: 1. Open the atlas and set up the view you want (a year, a regime profile, a place card, or a person's trajectory). The address bar always mirrors what you see. 2. Copy the URL and add `&embed=1`. 3. Paste it into an ` ``` The embedded map hides the site chrome and keeps only the map, a compact timeline, a title chip, an "Open in Jiangshan Atlas ↗" link, and a note that historical borders are approximate. Readers click once to start panning and zooming, so scrolling your page never gets stuck on the map. | Parameter | Effect | |---|---| | `embed=1` | Turn on embed mode (required) | | `year`, `polity`, `person`, `stop`, `trace`, `lang` | Same as the share links above | | `from=1072&to=1126` | Limit the timeline to this range; the timeline zooms to show only it | | `lock=1` | Freeze the map at `year` and hide the timeline | | `autoplay=1` | Play a person's trajectory stop by stop (with `person`), or play the timeline | WeChat Official Accounts, Zhihu, and Xiaohongshu do not allow iframes; share the plain link there instead. --- ## AI Agent, MCP & LLM Integration **Chronicles of the Realm** works out of the box as a **historical-geography visualization engine for LLMs, MCP Clients, and AI Agents**. Models **never need to guess latitude/longitude coordinates**—simply extract two semantic parameters from a poem or historical text, **`year`** and **`place`**, and the atlas automatically resolves ancient/modern place names, centers the camera, renders dynastic borders and multi-stop trajectories, and opens the **Trace Place** genealogy card: - **Machine-Readable Specification**: [`llms.txt`](llms.txt) - **Zero-Dependency Local MCP Server (`stdio`)**: [`scripts/mcp_server.js`](scripts/mcp_server.js) — add to Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, or Gemini CLI `mcpServers`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "jiangshan-atlas": { "command": "node", "args": ["/absolute/path/to/jiangshan-map/scripts/mcp_server.js"] } } } ``` Exposes 3 native MCP tools (`<5ms` offline response, zero npm dependencies): - `inspect_place({ year, place, lang? })`: Returns reigning monarch/era, controlling regime (`polity`), macro-region (`dao/lu/province`), prefecture (`jun/zhou/fu`), modern province/city, 2,400-year `lore`, and shareable deep-link URL. - `inspect_person({ person, stop?, lang? })`: Returns a historical figure or monarch's biography, chronological geocoded stops across dynasties, and shareable deep-link URL. - `search_atlas({ query, limit?, lang? })`: Searches across all ancient cities, poetic & battlefield landmarks, mountain passes, historical figures, imperial eras, and chronological milestones. - **Ready-to-Use Agent Skill**: [`skills/jiangshan-atlas/SKILL.md`](skills/jiangshan-atlas/SKILL.md) (includes the zero-dependency CLI renderer [`skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py`](skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py)) ```bash # Install into Claude Code / Gemini / Jetski global skills directory: mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills ~/.gemini/config/skills && cp -r skills/jiangshan-atlas ~/.claude/skills/ && cp -r skills/jiangshan-atlas ~/.gemini/config/skills/ ``` ### 1. Zero-Coordinate Dual-Parameter URL Protocol (0D Pinpoint / 1D Same-Year Route / 4D Multi-Year Route) | Mode | Example URL | Automatic Rendering Behavior | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Single-Point Pinpoint (0D)** | [`?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=819&place=蓝关&lang=en)
*(Han Yu's 819 CE exile poem at Languan Pass)* | Jumps to Tang Yuanhe 14 (819 CE), drops a pin on Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains, and opens its 2,400-year administrative genealogy card | | **Same-Year Multi-Stop Route (1D)** | [`?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=763&place=剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳&lang=en)
*(Du Fu's 763 CE poem on recapturing Henan & Hebei)* | Plots numbered vermilion arcs `1` → `5` across the 763 CE Tang map and auto-fits the viewport; click any stop to inspect its genealogy | | **Multi-Year Space-Time Route (4D)** | [`?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1079,1080,1094,1097&place=湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州&lang=en)
*(Su Shi's career across Huzhou, Huangzhou, Huizhou & Danzhou)* | Pairs `year[i]` with `place[i]`, labeling stops with their historical years and switching the underlying dynastic map whenever you click a stop | ### 2. CLI One-Command Screenshot & JSON Lookup (for Agent Tool Calls) ```bash # Single-point poetic landmark screenshot python3 skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py --year 819 --place 蓝关 --out /tmp/languan_819.png # Same-year multi-stop trajectory screenshot python3 skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py --year 763 --place 剑外,巴峡,巫峡,襄阳,洛阳 --out /tmp/dufu_763.png # Multi-year space-time trajectory screenshot python3 skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py --year 1079,1080,1094,1097 --place 湖州,黄州,惠州,儋州 --out /tmp/sushi_exile.png ``` ### 3. Browser JavaScript API (`window.atlasAPI`) & In-Browser WebMCP (`navigator.modelContext`) In browser automation environments (Playwright) or WebMCP-enabled AI browsers (`navigator.modelContext`), the page automatically registers `jiangshan_locate`, `jiangshan_inspect`, and `jiangshan_open_person`, and exposes `window.atlasAPI`: - `window.atlasAPI.locate({ year, place, zoom? })`: Drives the map to a single location or multi-stop trajectory and returns structured historical-geographic metadata. - `window.atlasAPI.inspect({ year, place, person?, stop? })`: Read-only query returning the controlling polity, ancient prefecture, modern province/city, leg distances, person events, and canonical shareable URL. - `window.atlasAPI.resolvePlace(place, year?)`: Resolves ancient and modern names for cities, strategic passes, poetic landmarks, and battlefields. - `window.atlasAPI.openPerson(person, stop?)` & `window.atlasAPI.search(query)`: Opens a person chronicle on the map or searches across the entire atlas. --- ## Run Locally No dependencies or build steps required. Clone and serve with any static HTTP server: ```bash git clone https://github.com/DeanChensj/jiangshan-map.git cd jiangshan-map python3 -m http.server 8000 ``` Then open `http://localhost:8000` in your browser. ## Run with Docker No local dependency needed. Build and start with Docker Compose: ```bash docker compose up -d --build ``` Then open `http://localhost:8008` (the port mapping `8008:80` is set in `docker-compose.yml`). The image is a plain `nginx:alpine` that serves this repository as static files: `Dockerfile` copies the working tree into `/usr/share/nginx/html`, and `.dockerignore` keeps the build context small by excluding `.git`, `.github`, `data/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, `skills/`, `workers/`, Markdown files, `geojson/demo.html` and the README demo images (`assets/hero_demo_*.webp`, `assets/preview_*.webp`) — the site does not need any of them at runtime. To use another port, change the `ports` mapping in `docker-compose.yml` (e.g. `"9000:80"`) and run `docker compose up -d` again. After pulling upstream changes, rebuild with `docker compose up -d --build`. Without Compose: `docker build -t jiangshan-map:latest .` then `docker run -d -p 8008:80 --name jiangshan-map jiangshan-map:latest`. Note: the image is built locally; it is not published to any registry. --- ## GeoJSON Export (for Leaflet / MapLibre / QGIS) The app ships its geometry as compact topology-deduplicated VLQ bundles. To use the vector layers in other projects, generate standard RFC 7946 GeoJSON (EPSG:4326, lon/lat) locally; the output goes to `geojson/` and is not committed. The export covers 403 BCE to 1948; later years and the modern province layer are not included. The prefecture layer (郡 / 州 / 府) is left out by default because it derives from CHGIS, whose terms forbid redistribution; add `--with-prefectures` to include it for local academic, non-commercial use, and do not publish the result. ```bash node scripts/export_geojson.js # or: node scripts/export_geojson.js node scripts/export_geojson.js --with-prefectures # adds the CHGIS-derived prefecture layer (local academic use only) ``` - `snapshots/.geojson` — one file per territorial phase; each feature has a `bbox` and `layer` (`polity` / `region`, plus `prefecture` with `--with-prefectures`), `title`, `title_en`, `category`, `tint`, `anchor`. - `index.json` — every dynasty's phases with `from` / `to` years (negative = BCE, no year 0) and the matching snapshot file. - `corridors.geojson` (walls, canals, roads, sea routes), `settlements.geojson`, `milestones.geojson`, `neighbors.geojson`, and `modern/` (rivers, lakes, hydro labels; `appear` / `vanish` give the years historical river courses and lakes are shown). To look up a point without loading every phase, use [`geojson/jiangshan-locate.js`](geojson/jiangshan-locate.js): it loads `index.json` plus only the snapshot covering the year, then runs a bbox-filtered point-in-polygon test. ```js const atlas = JiangshanLocate.create(); // or create({ base: '' }) const hit = await atlas.locate(118.78, 32.06, 1415); // lon, lat, year hit.polity.properties.title; // 明 hit.region.properties.title; // 南直隶 hit.prefecture; // null unless exported with --with-prefectures (then 应天府) ``` After exporting, serve the repository (`python3 -m http.server 8000`) and open `http://localhost:8000/geojson/demo.html` for a Leaflet example: drag the year slider, click the map, or open `demo.html?year=1415&lon=118.78&lat=32.06` to load, highlight and zoom automatically. Historical borders are schematic approximations, not surveyed boundaries. The data is GPL-3.0 except the prefecture-level boundaries; see [Data Sources & License](#data-sources--license). --- ## Data Sources & License Code and the data created by this project are released under **GPL-3.0**. One layer is not: the prefecture-level boundaries derived from CHGIS, which stay under CHGIS's own terms. | Layer | Source | License | | :-- | :-- | :-- | | Code (app, scripts, CLI, MCP server) | This project | GPL-3.0 | | Polity outlines (`polity`) | Started from [aourednik/historical-basemaps](https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps) (GPL-3.0), then redrawn by hand against historical texts | GPL-3.0 | | First-level divisions (`region`: 刺史部 / 道 / 路 / 省 …) | Drawn by hand from historical texts; the source of early versions was not recorded | GPL-3.0 | | **Prefecture-level boundaries** (`prefecture`: 郡 / 州 / 府, incl. Warring States and Qin commanderies) | Derived from **CHGIS V6** and the **Robert M. Hartwell China Historical GIS**, simplified to 0.01° and edited by hand | **Not GPL-3.0.** Academic, non-commercial use only; do not redistribute. See below | | Settlements, milestones, journeys, person chronicles, place lore | Compiled by this project from historical texts | GPL-3.0 | | Modern provinces | DataV GeoAtlas (Alibaba Cloud) | Subject to DataV GeoAtlas terms | | Rivers, lakes, neighbouring countries | Public-domain data | Public domain | | Terrain hillshade | Rendered by `scripts/build_terrain_tiles.py` from [AWS Terrain Tiles](https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/) (public-domain **SRTM**, **GMTED2010**, **ETOPO1**); only shaded images at no finer than about 1 km per pixel are published | GPL-3.0 (images) | | Guqin audio | Wikimedia Commons (*Liu Shui*, *Pingsha Luoyan*, *Yangguan Sandie*, *Zuiyu Changwan*, *Jiu Kuang*) | Public domain | **Scholarly references (not data sources).** Boundaries are checked against historical texts and Tan Qixiang's *The Historical Atlas of China* (谭其骧主编《中国历史地图集》). No map images or data from that atlas are included in this repository. **Prefecture-level boundaries (CHGIS).** This layer is not covered by GPL-3.0 and is shown here for non-commercial, educational use. Do not republish it from this repository; if you need prefecture boundaries, download CHGIS from its official distribution (Harvard Dataverse) under its terms. `scripts/export_geojson.js` leaves this layer out unless run with `--with-prefectures`. Cite it as: *CHGIS, Version: 6. © Fairbank Center for Chinese Studies of Harvard University and the Center for Historical Geographical Studies at Fudan University, 2016.* Provenance details: [data/atlas/README.md](data/atlas/README.md). **Approximate boundaries.** Historical territories and administrative boundaries are schematic approximations of broad jurisdictions, not surveyed borders. Do not cite them as precise or authoritative. **Reusing this project.** For the GPL-3.0 layers, credit **江山时序 Jiangshan Atlas** with a link to https://github.com/DeanChensj/jiangshan-map and cite the upstream sources above. Screenshots that show the prefecture layer carry the CHGIS terms as well. **Rights holders.** If you hold rights in any material here and believe it is used improperly, please [open an issue](https://github.com/DeanChensj/jiangshan-map/issues); we will respond and remove it if needed. **Contributing**: see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) ([中文贡献指南](CONTRIBUTING_ZH.md)) for repository structure, data conventions, and validation checks. **Report a data error**: found a wrong year, place or description? repositories.readme:
# Rakazo [English](./README.md) | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](./README.ja.md) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/elie222/rakazo?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&color=2563EB)](https://github.com/elie222/rakazo/stargazers) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-Join%20the%20community-5865F2?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/RWwKa2Sn7h) [![Download on the App Store](https://img.shields.io/badge/App%20Store-Download%20for%20iPhone-black?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://apps.apple.com/app/rakazo/id6801531099) [![Get Android on Google Play](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Play-Get%20the%20app-black?labelColor=black&style=for-the-badge&logo=googleplay&logoColor=white)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.rakazo.app) ![Rakazo — AI teammates you actually own](./docs/readme-hero.png) Rakazo is an open source, self-hosted alternative to Grok Bot. Persistent AI teammates with their own memory, routines, apps, and computer. Run it on your own machine, with your own model. Use it on the [web](https://app.rakazo.com), [desktop](https://rakazo.com/download/), [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/app/rakazo/id6801531099), and [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.rakazo.app). It is also an alternative to Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Instinct, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and Claude Duet. Learn more at [rakazo.com](https://rakazo.com). ## Features - Routines - Memory - Computer and browser use - Private or shared team computers - Sandboxes in Docker, the cloud, or on your own machine - Group chats - Delegation and subagents - Builds dashboards and docs you can share by link - Voice chat and calls - Any model, with your own keys - Thousands of app integrations, plus MCP
### Every bot gets a computer A browser, terminal, files, and a full desktop. Watch it work, take control to sign in, and hand it back. ### Bots that work together Put bots in a group and @mention them. They split the work, check each other, and report back.
### Routines Run a bot on a schedule, from an email, or from a webhook, and see every run. ### Pages Bots build live dashboards and documents you can open full screen, share, and ask about.
### Connected apps Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion, Linear and thousands more, plus your own MCP servers and OpenAPI tools. ### On every device Web, desktop, iPhone, iPad, and Android, all talking to the same server.
## Quick start (published images) You need Docker Engine, the Compose plugin, curl, and OpenSSL. No clone or Node install. ```bash mkdir -p rakazo && cd rakazo && curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elie222/rakazo/main/infra/compose/install-images.sh && bash install-images.sh ``` The installer downloads the Compose files, creates `.env` with random secrets, and starts Rakazo. It preserves an existing `.env` when rerun. Open [http://127.0.0.1:5173](http://127.0.0.1:5173), create an account, and connect a model. Local Docker computers are on by default. Optional remote providers: `e2b`, `novita`, `daytona`, `createos`, `boat`, `boxd`, `instabox`, or `railway` with the matching API key. Default image tag is `edge` (main builds, `linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`). Details and tags: [self-hosting guide](./docs/self-host.md#published-images-no-checkout). On restricted networks, override the installer download base (`RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_BASE`), skip existing Compose files (`--local` / `RAKAZO_DOWNLOAD_SKIP_EXISTING`), or mirror the bootstrap script URL — see [Restricted networks / mirror downloads](./docs/self-host.md#restricted-networks--mirror-downloads). For an agent-assisted install, use [SETUP_PROMPT.md](./SETUP_PROMPT.md). ## Run on a server Bots stay on when the backend runs on a server. Use the same installer on a VPS, then connect from the desktop app, the mobile app, or a browser. ```bash bash install-images.sh --prepare-only # edit .env: SANDBOX_PROVIDER=boat (or e2b / daytona / createos) with its API key, RAKAZO_HOST=your.domain bash install-images.sh ``` Put HTTPS in front of port 5173; [docs/self-host-production.md](./docs/self-host-production.md#public-single-vm-deployment) covers the Caddy setup and host hardening. In the desktop app choose **Existing instance** and enter the `https://` address. Or [deploy on Railway](https://railway.com/new/template/rakazo-template); see the [Railway setup guide](./infra/railway/README.md). ## Local development (source checkout) You need Node.js 24.15.0 or newer in the 24.x line, or Node.js 26+; pnpm 12; and Docker. Node.js 25.x is not supported. ```bash git clone https://github.com/elie222/rakazo.git cd rakazo cp .env.example .env ``` Set `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `POSTGRES_APP_PASSWORD` to two values from `openssl rand -hex 16`, then put them in `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` and `DATABASE_URL`. The app connects as its own `rakazo_app` login, which row-level security applies to; migrations run as the owner ([database roles](docs/self-host-configuration.md#database-roles)). Set `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, and `SCREEN_PROXY_SECRET` to independent long random values. Docker sandboxes also need a dedicated `SANDBOX_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN`. You can also set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, or connect a supported model provider during onboarding. For host-side development with Docker Desktop, set `SANDBOX_CONTROL_VIA_LOOPBACK=true` in `.env`. The supervisor discovers Docker Desktop's user socket automatically; `DOCKER_HOST` or `DOCKER_SOCKET` can override it for another Docker runtime. Managed app catalogs are optional. Set `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` for Composio, or the `PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_ID`, `PIPEDREAM_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `PIPEDREAM_PROJECT_ID` trio for Pipedream Connect. Users can add an HTTPS MCP server or OpenAPI JSON document from **Integrations** without enabling either managed catalog. Local (stdio) MCP servers are off until you set `MCP_STDIO_ENABLED=true` and list their commands in `MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_COMMANDS`; see [Tools and integrations](./docs/self-host-integrations.md). Connector credentials are encrypted on the server and are never returned by the API. Paid data services (map places, search results, work emails, profiles, SEO data) are optional too. Set `PAID_SERVICES_PROVIDER=treg` and `PAID_SERVICES_API_KEY` to an org-scoped [Treg](https://treg.to) token, and bots can find and call them on the deployment's account. When model credits are on, each call is charged to the organization's credits at the provider's cost plus 20%. ```bash pnpm install pnpm sandbox:build pnpm dev ``` `pnpm dev` uses the Postgres in `DATABASE_URL` when it accepts a connection. Otherwise it starts a local `rakazo-dev-postgres` container with Docker, and every checkout reuses that one. It applies migrations and generates the Prisma client before starting. A branch that adds migrations main doesn't have gets its own database on the same server, copied from the shared one when possible, so unmerged schema changes stay out of it. When the default ports are taken, for example by another git worktree, it moves to the next free block and prints the URL. Set `WEB_PORT` and `API_PORT` to choose ports yourself. To try a checkout from your phone or another computer, install [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com) on each device and set `RAKAZO_DEV_TAILNET=1` in `.env`. `pnpm dev` then serves the web app over HTTPS at `https://..ts.net:`, reachable only from devices on your tailnet, and stops serving it when you quit. Sign in at that URL on every device, including the one running it. The first run may ask you to turn on HTTPS certificates for your tailnet. To keep keys in a secrets manager instead of `.env`, set `RAKAZO_DEV_RUN_WITH` to the command that runs another with your secrets added, for example `op run --env-file=dev.env --` or `infisical run --env=dev --projectId= --`. `pnpm dev` then starts inside it, and the values it adds win over `.env`. To run Postgres from the Compose file instead, start it with the `postgres-host` overlay, which publishes loopback `127.0.0.1:5433`, and point `DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL` at it: ```bash docker compose --env-file .env \ -f infra/compose/docker-compose.yml \ -f infra/compose/docker-compose.postgres-host.yml \ up postgres -d ``` Use a URI-safe `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` (`openssl rand -hex 16`). An existing `pgdata` volume keeps the user, password, and database from first init, so keep those values in `.env`, or change them in place with `ALTER ROLE` / rename. Recreate the volume only after a backup (or when the data is disposable); `docker compose down -v` deletes all Postgres state. Open the printed URL ([http://127.0.0.1:5173](http://127.0.0.1:5173) by default), create an account, connect a model, and create your first bot. For deployment, provider selection, backups, and upgrades, see the [self-hosting guide](./docs/self-host.md), [production deployment](./docs/self-host-production.md), [backup and restore](./docs/self-host-backups.md), and [upgrading](./docs/self-host-upgrading.md). To use CreateOS, set `SANDBOX_PROVIDER=createos` and `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_API_KEY`. Optional `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_BASE_URL`, `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_SHAPE`, and `CREATEOS_SANDBOX_ROOTFS` default to `https://api.sb.createos.sh`, `s-2vcpu-2gb`, and `desktop:1`. To use Railway computers, set `SANDBOX_PROVIDER=railway`, `RAILWAY_API_TOKEN` and `RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_ID` on the API and worker. Choose the sandbox environment explicitly; Railway's automatic environment ID identifies the hosted app's environment. Use the narrowest Railway API token that works: prefer a project token if sufficient for sandbox operations and supported by the client's authentication. This provider currently uses bearer authentication, so use a team/workspace token rather than a personal account token. The live screen and desktop require `PRIVATE` networking so Railway's public domain can serve the screen. Computers use this mode and can reach other services in the same Railway project/environment, as well as the public internet. We recommend a dedicated Railway project (or at least a separate environment) for sandboxes, separate from the app and database. Recreate existing `ISOLATED` computers before use. The desktop is installed on first start. Stopping a computer saves its portable home and destroys the sandbox; the next start restores that home in a new sandbox. Railway sandbox usage is metered. New computers start in Railway's default region. Set `RAILWAY_SANDBOX_REGION` (for example `asia-southeast1-eqsg3a`) to keep them near the API; a running computer moves on its next start. Workspace exports reject files above 64 MiB without truncating them. Set `RAILWAY_MAX_WORKSPACE_FILE_BYTES` to change this limit. ## Desktop and mobile The Electron and Expo apps are clients of the same Rakazo API used by the web app. With the development stack running, launch Electron with: ```bash pnpm --filter @rakazo/desktop dev ``` On first run the desktop app asks whether to run Rakazo on this computer or connect to an existing server. **This computer** can run without Docker on Apple silicon Macs with macOS 26 or later when the build includes a server bundle. Fresh setups use this path: the app downloads the server and computer runtime as needed. Existing Docker setups are offered a move while Docker is running; choosing **Keep Docker** leaves them on Docker. Other builds and platforms use Docker Compose to install and start the published images (the same files as `infra/compose/install-images.sh`) under the app's data directory. This path needs Docker Desktop, OrbStack, or Docker Engine. Without one, setup offers the Docker Desktop download, opens an installed Docker app that is not running, and continues on its own once Docker answers. Installed builds pin the image tag to their own version; unpackaged builds pull `edge`. Developers running `pnpm dev` should pick **Existing instance** with `http://127.0.0.1:5173` instead. Public servers must use HTTPS; HTTP is accepted only for loopback and private LAN addresses (not link-local). The app verifies Rakazo's health endpoint before saving, and later launches go straight to that instance. The Docker stack keeps running after the app quits; the Docker-free server stops with the app. **Quit and Stop Bots** in the application menu stops the managed stack and quits; switching to another server also stops it. On Linux the desktop app ships as an AppImage, which needs FUSE 2 (`libfuse.so.2`). Distributions that only include FUSE 3, such as Fedora Silverblue or Ubuntu 24.04, show `dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2`. Install the FUSE 2 library (`fuse-libs` on Fedora, `libfuse2t64` on Ubuntu 24.04, `libfuse2` on older Ubuntu and Debian), or run the AppImage without FUSE: ```bash chmod +x Rakazo-*.AppImage ./Rakazo-*.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run ``` The Docker path of **This computer** looks for the `docker` CLI and does not detect Podman. To try another Docker-compatible CLI that supports the `compose` commands, set `RAKAZO_DOCKER_BINARY` to its path before starting the app. Use **Change Rakazo Server…** in the application menu to reconnect. Closing that window without saving returns to the previous instance. For development automation, set `RAKAZO_WEB_URL` to point the shell somewhere else without changing the saved instance, or `RAKAZO_FORCE_SETUP=1` to run setup again. Mobile build and release instructions live in [docs/mobile-release.md](./docs/mobile-release.md). ## UI language The web (and Electron-hosted) UI supports English, Deutsch, 한국어, Türkçe, हिन्दी, Português (Brasil), 简体中文, 繁體中文, Español, Русский, Français, עברית, Nederlands, 日本語, and Polski under **Settings → Language**. The Expo app ships the same 15 languages under **Account → Language**. A device language or `EXPO_PUBLIC_DEFAULT_UI_LOCALE` still selects the starting catalog before a saved choice. Native Electron setup and menus also support the web UI's languages, following the saved app choice or, on first launch, the system language. The marketing homepage (`apps/www`) offers all 15 languages through footer links, including `/zh/` and `/zh-tw/`; other marketing pages remain primarily English. ## Development ```text apps/ web, api, worker, desktop, mobile, and public website packages/ domain, contracts, persistence, adapters, UI, and test tooling infra/ local services and computer images docs/ architecture, operations, and release guides ``` Common checks: ```bash pnpm lint pnpm check pnpm test pnpm test:integration pnpm test:e2e ``` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for the development workflow and test matrix. ## Documentation Chinese guides cover [self-hosting](./docs/zh-CN/self-host.md), [models](./docs/zh-CN/self-host-models.md), [backups](./docs/zh-CN/self-host-backups.md), [upgrading](./docs/zh-CN/self-host-upgrading.md), and [restricted networks](./docs/zh-CN/self-host-restricted-network.md). - [Self-hosting](./docs/self-host.md) - [Self-host configuration](./docs/self-host-configuration.md) - [Self-host secrets](./docs/self-host-secrets.md) - [Sign-in and accounts](./docs/self-host-accounts.md) - [Models](./docs/self-host-models.md) - [Tools and integrations](./docs/self-host-integrations.md) - [Computer providers](./docs/self-host-sandbox-providers.md) - [Docker computers](./docs/self-host-docker-computers.md) - [Kubernetes / k3s installation](./docs/self-host-kubernetes.md) ([한국어](./docs/ko-KR/self-host-kubernetes.md)) - [Storage and encryption](./docs/self-host-storage.md) - [Production deployment](./docs/self-host-production.md) - [Backup and restore](./docs/self-host-backups.md) - [Upgrading](./docs/self-host-upgrading.md) - [Logs and monitoring](./docs/self-host-observability.md) - [Audit log](./docs/self-host-audit-log.md) - [Apps and clients](./docs/self-host-clients.md) - [Billing](./docs/self-host-billing.md) - [Computer runtime and isolation](./docs/computer-runtime.md) - [Desktop releases](./docs/desktop-release.md) - [Mobile releases](./docs/mobile-release.md) - [Performance testing](./docs/performance.md) - [Bots that manage bots](./docs/fleet-management.md) ## How Rakazo compares - [Grok Bot](https://rakazo.com/grok-bot-alternative/) - [Muse](https://rakazo.com/muse-alternative/) - [Dots](https://rakazo.com/dots-alternative/) - [Instinct](https://rakazo.com/instinct-alternative/) - [OpenClaw](https://rakazo.com/openclaw-alternative/) - [Hermes Agent](https://rakazo.com/hermes-alternative/) - [All comparisons](https://rakazo.com/alternatives/) ## Thanks - [Inbox Zero](https://getinboxzero.com/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) - [PromptLayer](https://promptlayer.com/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) - [ConnectorMap](https://connectormap.luinbytes.dev/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) - [CodeRabbit](https://www.coderabbit.ai/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) - [Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) - [Snyk](https://snyk.io/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) - [Incredibuild](https://www.incredibuild.com/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=rakazo_readme) ## Stack - TypeScript - React 19, Vite, and Tailwind CSS - Electron and Expo - Hono and oRPC - PostgreSQL and Prisma - Better Auth - Graphile Worker - Pi - Docker, E2B, Daytona, CreateOS, and Boat - Composio, Pipedream Connect, MCP, and OpenAPI integrations ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request. For security vulnerabilities, follow [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of filing a public issue. Rakazo is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](./LICENSE). Questions and ideas are welcome in the [Rakazo Discord community](https://discord.gg/RWwKa2Sn7h).

repositories.name: mailflare
repositories.description: Email for professionals and teams
repositories.readme:
# Mailflare A self-hosted alternative to Google Workspace. Setup **custom domain Emails**, **Calendar, Drive, Booking** and **built-in AI agents**. Run it on Cloudflare or Docker. Send and receive with Cloudflare, Resend or Amazon SES. Store files in R2, Backblaze B2 or AWS S3. Use D1, Postgres, MySQL or Turso for the database. [![Deploy to Cloudflare](https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/button)](https://deploy.workers.cloudflare.com/?url=https://github.com/hieunc229/mailflare) ## Screenshots

Inbox
Domains
Mailboxes

Calendar
Booking
Drive
### Sponsors   Want to support Mailflare? [Become a sponsor](https://store.paymug.co/buy/mailflare-sponsor). ## Features ### Apps - **Email**: Custom domain mailboxes, personal or shared, with access you control. Send and receive with Cloudflare Email, Resend or Amazon SES. - **Routing rules**: Store, forward, reject or sort incoming mail. - **Calendar**: Repeating events with time zones. Attendees get email invitations. - **Booking**: Share a public link so anyone can book a free time on your calendar. - **Drive**: Store and share files. - **AI agents**: Search mail, draft replies and manage events. Connect other AI tools over MCP. ### Technical - **Databases**: Cloudflare D1 (default), PostgreSQL, MySQL, Turso / libSQL, or a local SQLite file. Set `DATABASE_URL` to switch. Works with Supabase, Neon, PlanetScale, TiDB and more. See [Databases](docs/databases.md). - **File storage**: Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2 or AWS S3. - **Hosting**: Cloudflare Workers or a single Docker container. - **Admin**: Users, API keys, webhooks, audit logs and backups. - **Import**: Bring in mail from IMAP, Gmail Takeout, `.eml` and `.mbox` files. Mailflare currently supports 34 languages, including English, Português (Brasil), Português (Portugal), Español, Français, Deutsch, Italiano, Nederlands, Polski, Українська, Русский, Türkçe, 中文（简体）, 日本語, 한국어, Bahasa Indonesia, Bahasa Melayu, Tiếng Việt, ไทย, हिन्दी, বাংলা, मराठी, తెలుగు, தமிழ், ગુજરાતી, ಕನ್ನಡ, മലയാളം, ਪੰਜਾਬੀ, සිංහල, Kiswahili, Hausa, plus العربية, اردو and فارسی (right-to-left). ## Cost You can receive and send mail for free. - **Receiving**: Cloudflare Email Routing is free. - **Sending**: Use the free tier of Resend (3,000 emails a month) or Amazon SES. Cloudflare's own sending needs the $5/month Paid Worker plan. New Amazon SES accounts start in a sandbox. Ask AWS for production access to lift it. Prices change, so check [Resend](https://resend.com/pricing), [Amazon SES](https://aws.amazon.com/ses/pricing/) and [Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/). ## Deploy 1. **Deploy the app.** Click **Deploy to Cloudflare**. Keep the app name `mailflare`, or it will break. 2. **Finish setup.** Open the app at `/setup` and create your admin account. 3. **Connect a domain.** Add a domain from the same Cloudflare account, then create your first mailbox. > **`CF_TOKEN` is required.** Create a scoped [Cloudflare API token](https://github.com/hieunc229/mailflare/issues/24#issuecomment-5523686105) with these permissions: > > - All accounts: Email Sending:Edit, DNS Settings:Edit, Email Routing Addresses:Edit > - All zones: DNS Settings:Edit, Email Routing Rules:Edit, Zone Settings:Edit, DNS:Edit More options: [deployment guide](docs/deployment.md). ### Deploy with an AI agent Paste this into an AI agent that has terminal access (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and similar): ```text Install Mailflare for me from https://github.com/hieunc229/mailflare on my Cloudflare account. 1. Read README.md, docs/deployment.md and wrangler.jsonc first. 2. Ask me for my Cloudflare account ID and two API tokens, using a secret input: a deploy token (for Wrangler) and a runtime token (the Worker secret CF_TOKEN). Never print them, commit them, or pass them as command arguments. 3. Keep the Worker name exactly "mailflare". Create or reuse the D1 database "mailflare", the R2 bucket "mailflare-raw", and the queues "mailflare-inbound", "mailflare-outbound" and "mailflare-agent". 4. Install dependencies, run `npm run deploy`, and set CF_TOKEN as a Worker secret. Do not run remote database migrations yourself. The /setup page does that. 5. Give me the app URL and anything I still need to do. I will open /setup, create the admin account and connect my domain. ``` Token permissions and more options: [deployment guide](docs/deployment.md#deploy-with-an-ai-coding-agent). ### Self-host with Docker Runs as one container on any server, with SQLite and local files. ```bash cp .env.docker.example .env.docker docker compose up -d --build ``` See [self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md). ## Local development ```bash cp .dev.vars.example .dev.vars npm install npm run db:migrate:local npm run dev ``` Add your Cloudflare credentials to `.dev.vars`, then open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Run `npm run db:seed` to load sample data. - `npm run build`: build the Worker - `npm run deploy`: build and deploy - `npm run lint`: lint and type check A schema change needs a migration for each database type. See [Databases](docs/databases.md#migrations). ## Documentation - [Deployment and configuration](docs/deployment.md) - [Databases](docs/databases.md) - [Sending and receiving providers](docs/providers.md) - [API and integrations](docs/api.md) - [Email assistant and MCP](docs/email-assistant-and-mcp.md) - [Adding a language](docs/localization.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) ## License See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

repositories.readme:
# 🌐 God's Eye View **Official site: [godseyeview.ai](https://godseyeview.ai)** · [Download](https://godseyeview.ai/download/) · [Guide](https://godseyeview.ai/guide/) · [Releases](https://godseyeview.ai/releases/) · [Hosted version waitlist](https://godseyeview.ai/online/) · [Media](https://godseyeview.ai/press/) [![CI](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Reached #1 on GitHub Trending](https://img.shields.io/badge/%231_GitHub_Trending-thank_you!-F0A63C?style=flat-square&logo=github)](https://www.star-history.com/?type=date&repos=bilawalsidhu%2Fgods-eye-view) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view?style=flat-square&color=4fe3ff)](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/stargazers) [![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-4fe3ff?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) ### A spy-satellite simulator in your browser. Except the data is real. _The window through which we see our world._ [![God's Eye View: a live 3D globe indexing the planet's public signals](docs/media/site/hero.webp)](https://godseyeview.ai) Click any satellite, plane, ship or public camera and you can track it. Turn on FLIR mode and suddenly you're wondering, holy crap, is this real? And it's free, and open source. **[One-click install with Pinokio](https://pinokio.co/apps/github-com-bilawalsidhu-gods-eye-view)** · **[Run it from the terminal](#-quick-start)** · **[Hosted version waitlist](https://godseyeview.ai/online/)** 🏆 **#1 on GitHub Trending**, daily and weekly · **[#8 Product of the Day](https://www.producthunt.com/products/god-s-eye-view?launch=god-s-eye-view)**, hunted by Chris Messina · _“pretty cool”_ — [Brendan Eich](https://x.com/BrendanEich/status/2094592096401490266), creator of JavaScript · Featured on **[Pinokio](https://pinokio.co/posts/01m1m4p9xxm3qw7dnnpj2wr93g)** ▶️ **From the project behind the God's Eye View series** _(formerly WorldView)_ — [25M+ views on YouTube](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PL6qSg2I-7_koPbDnSMo0QeeHX_RknA2uv&si=nBGYMoHWQw41v93Q) **As seen on** [Matt Wolfe](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S2VJU5DQqlU) · [Riley Brown](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NR_GMq2lDCE) · [Digg](https://digg.com/tech/r7whv988) · [The Escapist](https://www.escapistmagazine.com/news-gods-eye-view-spy-satellite-simulator-setup-focus-keyphrase-gods-eye-view/) · [UNILAD Tech](https://www.uniladtech.com/social-media/youtube/viewers-concerned-youtubers-safety-built-gods-eye-monitor-889810-20260309) · [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/video/the-stream/2026/3/8/how-do-you-track-a-war-in-real-time) · [NDTV](https://www.ndtv.com/video/strait-of-hormuz-news-hormuz-stranglehold-no-end-in-sight-1080351) · [Mojo Story](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UXkJjyFfrwc) · [all media](https://godseyeview.ai/press/)
---
**[Quick Start](#-quick-start) · [What It Does](#️-what-this-thing-does) · [First Five Minutes](#-the-first-five-minutes) · [Talk to It](#️-talk-to-it) · [What's Live](#️-whats-on-the-globe) · [Keys & Costs](#-api-keys) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)**
--- ## 🌍 Why This Exists God's Eye View brings public signals into one explorable globe. Track the world live. Talk to it. Break it. Extend it. Flight transponders, ship beacons, orbital elements, seismographs, and public cameras already tell us a lot about the world. God's Eye View puts them in the same place, so you can move between a global picture and an individual aircraft, ship, or street. It runs locally in your browser, with source code you can inspect and extend. > Half the magic is that it looks like a forbidden cockpit. The other half is that every line of code is inspectable. Most feeds are live or regularly refreshed. Traffic is simulated along real roads using aggregate location data. CCTV camera poses and rocket launch trajectories are coarse estimates. Start with the included data sources, then add your own. Each layer is a separate module. --- ## 🎛️ What This Thing Does The world is already broadcasting. We fuse it together into a 3D globe for you and your agents. We've got a plurality of sensor systems watching the planet right now. Satellite imagery, flights, ships, weather, public cameras. Each captures a sliver of what's happening. God's Eye View pulls that treasure trove of public data into a single picture.

Ask the planet
Use voice to ask the planet questions in natural language, and it annotates the 3D globe with the answer.
Flights and vessels
Click on a satellite, plane, ship or public camera and you can track it.
Satellites
Toggle on different kinds of satellites, everything from GPS to Starlink.

Public cameras
Some layers, like traffic and camera poses, are estimates, and the app says so.
Cockpit
Visualize a flight from the third-person perspective and jump into a rendered cockpit view.
World class weather
Clouds, rain radar, lightning density and cyclone tracks with forecast cones. And since we say 4D, you can scrub the cloud imagery backwards in time.

Recent imagery
Draw a bounding box around a fire and it'll retrieve the Sentinel-2 images, draped on the 3D terrain. All keyless, ladies and gentlemen.
Transit
Click a bus in Boston and it starts leaving a trail. This might be the most overkill way to track your bus.
RF and SDR support
Now you can connect your own SDR and visualize everything you're detecting. The SDR nerds know all the other possibilities.

World radio
Ask for radio near anywhere and the globe starts broadcasting. Drag the tuner across up to 750 stations.
MCP server
We've built MCP access so your agents can query the same picture and add their findings to a shared canvas.
Director Mode
Draw outlines, sketch paths, drop your annotations on the map.
Everything else it does - **🛩️ Cockpit view:** Ride inside a tracked flight — the camera holds the terrain under you all the way down. - **📡 Contacts:** A 250 km roster of everything near your target — step through live aircraft and drop into any cockpit. - **🎯 Click-to-track anything:** Camera locks on, draws a fading trail, surfaces full metadata — and a tracked fire or vessel hands you off to the nearest live camera in one click. - **🖊️ Voice whiteboard:** Speak annotations onto the world — real boundary polygons, marks, and routes. - **🛫 3D fleet:** 122 procedural models drawn life size by type — airliners, business jets, helicopters, drones, ships, buses, trams and trains — and every contact swaps from glyph to 3D model as you close in. - **🎨 Reskin reality:** GLSL sensor looks over the normal globe — CRT, NVG, FLIR/thermal, Noir. - **🟩 Detection overlay:** Screen-space bounding boxes and IDs on everything in view. - **🎖️ Military HUD:** Tactical heads-up display with intelligence-style telemetry. - **🌐 Global Context:** Stage the full situational picture with one switch — and get your exact view back when you leave. - **🎥 Scene director:** Capture cinematic camera tours for clips and demos. - **🔗 Share Links:** Camera, style, layers, and even one tracked target serialize into a URL — a live target is a handoff, not a bookmark. - **🏠 Reset Globe:** One control — or one sentence — back to the full Earth. - **🌦️ Weather:** Animate GFS or ECMWF forecast wind, replay observed radar, satellite clouds and lightning on one timeline, and follow NHC/CPHC cyclone tracks. No key needed. - **📷 Mapped ALPR cameras:** License-plate-reader camera locations tagged in OpenStreetMap, one city at a time. Locations and tags only; no key needed. - **🔭 Satellite passes:** Ask by voice when any loaded satellite next rises over you: rise, peak and set times, and whether you can see it. - **🔎 Analyst answers:** Count, filter and rank satellites, datacenters and dams by voice, alongside flights, ships, fires and quakes; answers say when a feed is stale or on a fallback. - **🧭 Tilt and North Up:** Switch between straight-down and a 35° oblique, or put north at the top, while a tracked target stays centered. - **🔍 Keyless search:** Type decimal coordinates, a two-dimensional WGS84 `geo:` URI (for example, `geo:39.7392,-104.9903`), or a bundled city or landmark to fly there with no geocoder request; other names use Google when configured, then Photon and Nominatim. - **📦 Shareable scenes:** Import, preview and share Director scenes as files or bundles, with camera anchors, authored moves and data packs. - **🌊 Nepal flood scene:** Replay the Bhote Koshi flood: flood path, witness sources and before-and-after imagery (bundled data is non-commercial; see [DATA_SOURCES.md](DATA_SOURCES.md)).
